title: A Lost Maya City Hidden in the Jungle for 1,000 Years
mediaSource: lost Maya city Minanbe Yucatan jungle pyramid archaeology

scenes.title: An entire city was hiding in the jungle
scenes.narration: Deep in Mexico's Yucatán jungle, archaeologists discovered a Maya city that had remained abandoned and largely untouched for about a thousand years.

scenes.title: There was no road to reach it
scenes.narration: The team had to cut through kilometers of dense forest to reach the site, inspiring the name Minanbé, meaning there is no path.

scenes.title: Palaces and temples were waiting inside
scenes.narration: The site contains monuments with carved reliefs, palatial buildings, and large temples, showing that it was a substantial urban center.

scenes.title: One pyramid rises about 12 meters
scenes.narration: One of the major structures is a pyramid around forty feet, or roughly twelve meters, tall.

scenes.title: The jungle protected it after abandonment
scenes.narration: After the city was abandoned, dense vegetation covered the architecture and made the area extremely difficult to access.

scenes.title: No road may be why the city survived
scenes.narration: The jungle caused the city to disappear from view, but it also protected many of its remains. Archaeologists are now beginning to reconstruct the story of Minanbé.
